about.title: Greenfield Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Greenfield is a small, close-knit Monterey County city, but its shops, agricultural facilities, and apartment complexes carry the same legal obligations to keep floors, stairways, and walkways safe as anywhere else in California. When a property owner near Elm Avenue or Walnut Avenue lets a spill sit, ignores a broken step, or ignores poor lighting in a parking area, someone eventually gets hurt. California law doesn't automatically hold an owner responsible just because a fall happened on their property — the injured person generally has to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn about it. That's why what happens in the hours and days after a fall matters. Photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage can make or break a claim later. LawProactive doesn't handle claims directly, but we can connect you with an independent attorney who works on contingency and can help you sort out what evidence matters most for your situation.

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: Because California requires showing the owner knew or should have known about the hazard, an attorney can help pinpoint what proof — cleaning logs, prior complaints, or timing — actually supports that.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Greenfield businesses recycle their surveillance footage within days or weeks, so an early request to preserve it can be the difference between having evidence and having none.

items.title: Your Own Fault Isn't the End of It
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover even if you were partly responsible for the fall, though your share of fault can reduce the final amount.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Greenfield?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a public building or sidewalk maintained by a city or county entity, the deadline to act is much shorter. An attorney can help confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What should I do right after falling at a store on El Camino Real or Oak Avenue?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of the exact spot where you fell, including any spill, debris, or damaged flooring, before it gets cleaned up. Ask an employee to document the incident and get names of anyone who saw it happen. Seeking medical attention promptly also creates a record connecting your injury to the fall.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, the connection service is free. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to find out whether your situation is worth pursuing.
